newsitem.title: FRANCE: Analysts expect weak Pechiney H1 results, 96 loss.
newsitem.headline: Analysts expect weak Pechiney H1 results, 96 loss.

text.p: Analysts expect sluggish aluminium markets to weigh on the first half results of aluminium and packaging giant Pechiney.
Pechiney, which swung back to profit in 1995 -- the year of its privatisation -- may be in the red again in full year 1996 due to provisions linked to its Challenge cost cutting plan, they predicted.
On September 19 Pechiney is due to release its first half accounts and detail its keenly-awaited Challenge plan.
The plan is aimed at raising profitability to the levels of Pechiney's best competitors in all its sectors and to meet investment needs without further raising debt.
"We are not very optimistic. Things are not looking great with the exception of one or two businesses," an analyst for brokerage firm Pinatton told Reuters.

Analysts predict net profit excluding extraordinary items of between 300 and 350 million francs ($58.3 and $68 million) in the first half of 1996. Pechiney reported a net profit of 658 million francs in the first half of 1995.

But analysts said Pechiney's earnings in the first half of 1995 were helped by firm aluminium prices, a favourable economic environment in Europe and the strong performance of its international trade operations.
Already published sales data for the first half of 1996 show all this has changed, analysts said.
Packaging sales were stable but aluminium sales slumped 9.7 percent and international trade 7.1 percent in the first half of 1996.
In the beverage can sector sales volume are growing in Europe but lower prices are eating up margins in the United States.
Slow demand pushed aluminium metal prices to fresh two-year lows this week, with traders saying that if stocks on the London Metal Exchange continue to rise support at $1,400 may be tested.
Aluminium was last seen at these levels in August 1994. it reached a peak of $2,195 in January 1995.
"Even if aluminium prices pick up later on it will be too late for 1996," one analyst said.
Aluminium demand is expected to rebound in 1997 but one analyst said that because next year's primary aluminium supply contracts are being negotiated at current prices "1997 is not starting well".
In a June interview with French weekly Investir, Chairman Jean-Pierre Rodier said that 1996 profits before extraordinary items may remain unchanged from 1995.
He said that while macroeconomic factors looked good, it was still unclear when this would help into sales volume.
Pechiney reported a 1995 net profit of 1.465 billion francs but this included 730 million francs of gains linked to the sale of assets.
For full year 1996, analysts predict a net profit before extraordinary items of some 700 million francs.
But between 1.0 to 1.5 billion francs of provisions linked to Challenge are expected to be included into second half accounts 1996, propelling Pechiney into the red in 1996, analysts said.
Investors and analysts eagerly await details of the Challenge plan, which may cut between 3,000 and 3,500 jobs by end 1998. Pechiney employs 37,000 people worldwide of which 19,000 in France.
The plan is aimed at cutting costs by 1.5 to 3.0 billion francs but Rodier is expected to fine-tune that estimate on Thursday.
"What we really want to know is how and by how much Challenge will reduce costs," one analyst said.
-- Paris newsroom +331 4221 5432 ($ = 5.146 French Francs)
